title: Divisions of the Bible
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The learner identifies the two divisions of the Bible (Old Testament, before Jesus; New Testament, from Jesus) and categorises books into their groups (Law, History, Poetry and Wisdom, Prophets; Gospels, Acts, Letters, Revelation).

floor.prerequisite: Can sort books into the two Testaments.
floor.question: Is Acts in the Old or New Testament?

representations: a library drawn with labelled shelves
contexts: finding a reading quickly in church

board.do: Draw two bookcases: Old Testament and New Testament, with labelled shelves.

board.say: Which shelf does Romans go on?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say New Testament letters.

misconceptions.ask: How many divisions has the Bible?
misconceptions.repair: Name the two divisions; note that some Bibles add the deuterocanonical books, which the learner's church will explain.
Remember: Old Testament before Jesus, New Testament from Jesus. Genesis is the start of the Old.
Matthew opens the New Testament with Jesus' family line. Open the Bible to show it.

misconceptions.ask: In which group of books is Psalms?
misconceptions.repair: Draw a library: Law, History, Poetry and Wisdom, Prophets; Gospels, Acts, Letters, Revelation. Place books on shelves.

checks.question: How many divisions has the Bible?
checks.answer: Two: the Old and New Testament

checks.question: In which group of books is Psalms?
